claims.text: A 'lane' is a path by which a model's output becomes a file on disk: the local Ollama lane, the paid DeepSeek lane, the Claude CLI lane.
claims.why: This chunk does not define any lane; it only re-exports checks. The claim refers to external modules not present in this chunk.

claims.text: On 2026-07-30 that cost the repo three modules: two new guards (content substitution, invented first-party imports) went into providers/deepseek.py and, within the same hours, not into providers/ollama.py; the external, untrusted, PAID lane was therefore strictly safer than the local, free, DEFAULT one, for the two failure modes that had just been measured.
claims.why: This chunk does not contain the referenced files (providers/deepseek.py, providers/ollama.py) or any history. The claim cannot be verified from this code.

claims.text: The baseline lives here, every lane calls run_checks instead of writing its own sequence, and a lane may ADD checks but may never skip the baseline.
claims.why: This chunk exports run_checks but does not contain any lane code that calls it. No enforcement of 'may never skip' is visible.

claims.text: What deliberately does NOT move here: claims about a specific model. The elision markers are a statement about what one vendor's model emits when it truncates, and two lanes must stay free to disagree about that without silently re-tuning each other's guard. Those arrive as policy; the baseline is shared.
claims.why: This chunk does not define any policy or model-specific claims. The claim is about design intent, not verifiable from this code.
